# Error Codes and Troubleshooting — facts

> Source-anchored units about Error Codes and Troubleshooting: 26 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Definitions

- [statement] A server-selection timeout means the driver could not select a suitable server within its selection budget. Investigate topology and underlying exceptions; the headline alone does not establish a network outage. Read preference and server eligibility also affect selection. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md, https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md

## How it works

- [statement] A Mongoose buffered-operation timeout can occur when a model belongs to an unconnected connection, even if another connection succeeded. Verify the model's connection and await it; disabling bufferCommands can expose missing connection setup. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/faq.md
- [statement] Mongoose buffers model calls before connection. When operations appear to hang, check connection initialization and model binding; disabling bufferCommands can expose connection mistakes. (low confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Troubleshooting must distinguish server error codes from client connection failures: the server code reference interprets mongod/mongos errors, while Mongoose also exposes driver server-selection failures and model-operation buffering failures. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/error-codes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md
- [statement] In Mongoose, inspect the error reason and reason.servers descriptions. A replica-set member advertising localhost can produce ECONNREFUSED even when the application URI uses remote hostnames; inspect rs.conf() member addresses. (low confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] Collect the complete exception and stack trace, credentials-redacted connection string, driver and server versions, DNS lookup output, connectivity tests, and relevant logs before escalating a server-selection failure. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout.md
- [statement] The retryable-writes specification uses RetryableWriteError labels to determine retryability. Matching an arbitrary exception message or retrying every server error is not an equivalent implementation of this protocol. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] The retry budget depends on timeout configuration: ordinary retryable writes allow one retry, while client-side operation timeout through timeoutMS can permit additional attempts until success, a non-retryable error, or budget expiry. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] NoWritesPerformed indicates no write was performed. MongoDB documents this label beginning in 6.1; the driver specification also preserves an error indicating a write attempt when later failures are known no-ops, so final-error handling must retain outcome uncertainty. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] MongoDB distinguishes Unauthorized (13), AuthenticationFailed (18), MaxTimeMSExpired (50), WriteConflict (112), NotWritablePrimary (10107), and DuplicateKey (11000). Preserve the numeric code and symbolic name when classifying a failure; these identify different error categories. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/error-codes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/base/error_codes.yml
- [statement] Mongoose initial connection failure rejects mongoose.connect(); handle that promise with catch or try/catch. After connection, observe error and disconnected events. An error event alone does not cover every loss of connectivity. (low confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] Starting with MongoDB 6.1, NoWritesPerformed can establish that a failed retryable write performed no writes. Preserve partial bulk results and error context; a generic failure or absence of that label does not establish that nothing changed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Server-selection timeouts mean the driver could not find a suitable server in time. Investigate nested errors and topology information alongside deployment availability, network rules, DNS, TLS, and authentication rather than treating the timeout alone as a root cause. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md
- [statement] DuplicateKey (11000) indicates a violated unique index. Diagnose the indexed fields and rejected values rather than assuming every duplicate-key error concerns _id. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/base/error_codes.yml · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/
- [statement] Use driver retry eligibility and error labels rather than retrying every exception. MongoDB retryable-write execution preserves its session/transaction identity; an application issuing a fresh write does not automatically preserve that identity. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB's source definitions map 13 to Unauthorized, 18 to AuthenticationFailed, 50 to MaxTimeMSExpired, 112 to WriteConflict, 121 to DocumentValidationFailure, and 11000 to DuplicateKey. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/base/error_codes.yml · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] For duplicate-key failures, inspect the actual unique index. Mongoose's unique schema option requests an index; it does not itself enforce uniqueness before the index exists. Tests that recreate a database can await Model.init() before asserting duplicate rejection. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/faq.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/base/error_codes.yml, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/
- [statement] For local connections refused at ::1:27017, Mongoose documents an IPv6 localhost mismatch. Using 127.0.0.1 or enabling server IPv6 support addresses that specific configuration problem. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/faq.md
- [statement] For mongodb+srv DNS failures, run nslookup -type=SRV _mongodb._tcp.<cluster-name>.mongodb.net from the application host. Verify the hostname, returned records, DNS provider support, and outbound DNS access before changing connection settings. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout.md
- [statement] Retryable writes require an eligible deployment and acknowledged operations. Standalones, unacknowledged writes, and multi-document updateMany/deleteMany operations do not receive ordinary retryable-write protection; transaction statements are not individually retryable. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] Application-level re-execution of a write needs idempotency analysis. AWS's DocumentDB example shows repeated $inc changing a counter repeatedly, while MongoDB's retryable-write protocol reuses the transaction identity to provide at-most-once execution; those are different retry mechanisms. (medium confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-2-exception-handling/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] Elastic issue 4541 reports an instrumentation bug in APM Java agent 1.55.1/1.56.0: closing a cached shared JAR could kill MongoDB monitor class loading, leaving the client CONNECTING and ending in MongoTimeoutException. The issue includes ZipFile closed and NoClassDefFoundError traces and a maintainer-confirmed fix, providing a concrete non-network timeout diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://github.com/elastic/apm-agent-java/issues/4541 · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] For connection diagnosis, check deployment availability, outbound TCP access, Atlas IP access rules, DNS SRV resolution, and TLS certificate configuration. Correlate driver discovery logs with incoming-connection evidence in server logs. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/server-selection-timeout/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] An ordinary unique single-field index treats missing and explicit null values as a null index key, permitting only one such entry. A unique partial index constrains only documents matching its filter; choose that filter to reflect the intended optional-field semantics. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
- [statement] Retryable writes require an eligible replica-set or sharded deployment and acknowledged writes; standalone deployments and w:0 writes do not qualify. Writes inside a transaction are not individually retried by retryWrites. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] AWS DocumentDB exception-handling guidance illustrates a general application-retry hazard: a lost response can leave the write outcome unknown, and issuing a fresh non-idempotent increment may apply it twice. Its sample mitigation uses operation identifiers and conditional updates; this is DocumentDB guidance, not proof of MongoDB server behavior. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-2-exception-handling/ · keywords: Error Codes and Troubleshooting
